ai.text:
This proposal would put into EU law the fishing rules set by the North Pacific Fisheries Commission (NPFC), the body created by a convention that entered into force on 19 July 2015 to manage high seas fish stocks in the North Pacific. The EU is a party to that convention, and the NPFC's rules bind the Union. For the first time, the proposed Regulation would implement the NPFC measures adopted between 2015 and 2026 that apply to EU fishing vessels in the convention area. The European Parliament and the Council would decide on it together, on an equal footing.

The stated aims are to let the EU act quickly on rules affecting its fleet, to give operators a level playing field, and to support the long-term sustainable management of fish stocks.

On protecting marine life, the proposal covers sharks, including a ban on shark finning, and requires reporting of accidental catches of sharks. It also covers anadromous fish, which are species that migrate between fresh and salt water, with reporting of their accidental catches. Fishers would have to retrieve abandoned, lost or otherwise discarded gear, and the release of plastics and other marine pollution would be prohibited.

The proposal also sets out monitoring and control measures. These include rules for monitoring chub mackerel, marking vessels, and using vessel monitoring systems. It sets rules for transshipments and transfers at sea, for monitoring them in port, and for reporting the target species involved. It also covers enforcement, boarding and inspection on the high seas, including the definition of serious violations, and measures against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

Finally, the proposal includes provisions on reporting obligations, confidentiality and data protection. It also lists powers that would be delegated to the European Commission, covering matters such as chub mackerel catch monitoring, technical specifications for tracking devices, reporting timing, transshipment monitoring including a regional observer programme, and duties of the master of a fishing vessel during boarding and inspection.
